What if an air bubble got into your vein?
Movies say one bubble kills you instantly.
Truth? A tiny bubble is usually harmless.
IV drips often sneak a few in.
Your blood carries it to your heart.
The heart pumps it straight to your lungs.
And your lungs are a giant bubble filter.
Millions of tiny vessels trap it.
Then the air slowly dissolves away.
But a big rush of air is different.
It can foam up inside your heart.
Like an air lock jamming a pump.
So nurses flick bubbles out of IV lines.
And IV pumps sound an air alarm.
Doctors give pure oxygen to shrink bubbles.
Some patients even go into pressure chambers.
Divers get bubbles too. It's called the bends.
So... did you believe the movie myth?
